headline: New Amazon Reserve Marks 70 Million Acres Protected
meta_description: NGO Rainforest Trust celebrates 70 million acres of rainforest protection, with a new 715,000-acre reserve in Bolivia serving as a critical wildlife corridor.
summary_short: A new wildlife reserve along Bolivia's Iténez River protects jaguars, river dolphins, and 260 fish species—marking a major milestone for rainforest conservation.
body:
The Rainforest Trust has reached a conservation milestone: 70 million acres of rainforest protected worldwide—an area roughly the size of Nevada. The achievement accelerated dramatically in recent months, with 10 million of those acres added in just eight months, driven largely by work in South America. At the heart of this progress sits the newly created Agua Dulce Municipal Wildlife Reserve in Bolivia, a 715,000-acre expanse along the Iténez River that scientists call a "link of life." This 780-mile-long waterway, which forms much of the border between Bolivia and Brazil, harbors jaguars, Amazon river dolphins, giant otters, and 260 species of fish—25 of which exist nowhere else on Earth. The reserve functions as a transboundary corridor, stitching together protected areas across both nations and allowing wildlife to migrate freely through the ecosystem.

Local partner Faunagua led the reserve's creation with Rainforest Trust's technical and financial backing, ensuring that protections balanced three pillars: wildlife flourishing, ecosystem services, and sustainable economic opportunities for surrounding communities. The reserve encompasses Amazonian forests, floodplains, pampas, and riparian ecosystems—some of the most biodiverse habitat in the greater Amazon.

The timing of this success reflects broader conservation momentum. Brazilian authorities recently reported that Amazon deforestation has fallen to its lowest recorded rate, signaling that determined action against tree-felling can work. For Rainforest Trust's leadership, the 70-million-acre milestone represents not an endpoint but a clarion call. As the world approaches 2030 and global pledges to protect 30 percent of the planet, the organization remains focused on safeguarding the most imperiled ecosystems where conservation yields the greatest gains for species, ecosystems, and people alike.
quick_facts: 715,000-acre wildlife reserve created in Bolivia along Iténez River
70 million acres of rainforest protected by Rainforest Trust globally
Iténez River home to 260 fish species, 25 found nowhere else
10 million acres added to protection in just 8 months
